notes: Beginning of the second Coates letter, dated exactly 6.1.1966, pencil folio 47. Its year is retained without reconciling it with 4.1.67 on scan 044. It gives two further formulations of C and starts an inverse-polynomial argument. The heading subscript is inked and has the plain typed 1 form, while five other subscripts have the crossed χ form. The cancelled i in motive-theorietically is explicit. In the formula, the bases are u and the exponents b, b−1. The declared maps are u:B→A and v:A→B, with A=H^i(X), B=H^(2n−i)(X), and w=u∘v:A→A. Thus the endomorphism to which the characteristic polynomial of w applies is the displayed composition w; no identification changing the two printed u bases is inserted into the transcription. The inverse-polynomial step for this w was checked: put p_w(t)=det(tI−w)=tq(t)+c0. Cofactor expansion gives adj(tI−w)(tI−w)=p_w(t)I; coefficient comparison followed by right multiplication by the corresponding powers of w telescopes to p_w(w)=0. The constant term c0=(-1)^b det(w) is nonzero for the page’s automorphism w. Therefore w[−q(w)/c0]=I, giving w^−1=−q(w)/c0, with the stated coefficient ratios and signs. This verifies the linear-algebra step for w; it does not prove the entire motive-theoretic equivalence. The written u bases remain unchanged.
